title: Dependency graph and SBOMs
goal: Explain where dependency data comes from and how to export it.
points: The graph comes from four sources: static analysis of manifest and lock files, Dependabot graph jobs (Go and Python), **automatic dependency submission**, and the **dependency submission API**.
Automatic dependency submission covers Maven, Gradle, NuGet, pip and Poetry. It runs in GitHub Actions and uses Actions minutes.
The submission API is `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependency-graph/snapshots`. Use it for build-time dependencies a manifest can't show.

**SBOM:** Insights > Dependency graph > Export SBOM, or the REST API. Format: SPDX JSON. Read access is enough. The synchronous `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependency-graph/sbom` endpoint stops working after 2026-11-13; use the async generate-report and fetch-report pair.
Dependabot alerts come from the graph matched against GitHub-reviewed advisories.
trap: The SBOM export format is SPDX, not CycloneDX.
tryIt: Open **Insights > Dependency graph** on any repo and select Export SBOM.

details.title: Where the data comes from

head: Source
Covers
Notes
rows: Manifests and lock files; transitive dependencies for Maven, npm, pnpm and Yarn
Indirect dependencies inferred from a manifest without a lock file are left out of vulnerability checks
No Actions minutes; uses Dependabot secrets for private registries; skips packages it can't reach; not on GHES
Runs in Actions when a default-branch commit changes a manifest; setting: Enabled, or Enabled for labeled runners (label `dependency-submission`, Linux or macOS)
Highest precedence; shows in dependency review but not in org dependency insights

points: Precedence per manifest: user submissions, then Dependabot graph jobs, then automatic submission, then static analysis.
Community-maintained ecosystems: Julia, OpenTofu, pub.

details.title: Ecosystems and files (module 2)
points: Supported: Cargo, Composer, NuGet, GitHub Actions workflows, Go modules, Maven, npm, pip, pnpm, pub, Poetry, RubyGems, Swift PM, Yarn.

Lock files give the most accurate graph: Cargo.lock, composer.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, Gemfile.lock, poetry.lock, pubspec.lock, Package.resolved. Maven uses pom.xml, Go uses go.mod.
Direct dependencies are declared or submitted; indirect (transitive) ones come from lock files. Manifest-only means indirect dependencies aren't checked for vulnerabilities.

The graph updates on pushes to the default branch that change a supported manifest or lock file, and when a dependency's own repo changes. Submitted dependencies show which detector submitted them and when.

Two tabs: **Dependencies** (upstream) and **Dependents** (downstream). Dependents show only for public repos; the "Used by" badge needs more than 100 dependents. Filters: `ecosystem:` and `relationship:direct|transitive|inconclusive`.

details.title: The submission API
points: Required body: `version`, `job` (`id`, `correlator`), `sha` (up to 64 chars), `ref`, `detector` (`name`, `version`, `url`), `scanned`. `metadata` allows up to 8 scalar keys.
Resolved entries use `package_url` (a PURL), `relationship` direct or indirect, and `scope` runtime or development.
Only the latest snapshot per `job.correlator` plus `detector.name` counts. A successful call returns 201. Classic tokens need the `repo` scope; in Actions the job needs `contents: write`.
Pair it with dependency review by submitting first and retrying the review while the `x-github-dependency-graph-snapshot-warnings` header is non-empty.

details.title: SBOM export
points: SPDX format; the REST API returns SPDX JSON. UI path: Insights > Dependency graph > Export SBOM.

Async flow: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependency-graph/sbom/generate-report` returns 201 with an `sbom_url`; then `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependency-graph/sbom/fetch-report/{sbom_uuid}` answers 202 while processing and 302 to a temporary download URL when ready. Reports are kept up to one week.
The old synchronous `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependency-graph/sbom` is deprecated and won't be accessible after November 13, 2026.
Why it matters: US federal suppliers must provide an SBOM under Executive Order 14028 (module 2).

details.title: Dependency insights (organization)
points: Enterprise Cloud only, needs the dependency graph, excludes private dependencies, and is in maintenance mode.
Visibility: org Settings > Member privileges > "Allow members to view dependency insights" (default: all members), or the enterprise policy "Dependency insights visibility".

title: Dependabot alerts, severity and EPSS
goal: Read a Dependabot alert and prioritize it using severity and EPSS.
points: Alerts fire when a dependency matches a **GitHub-reviewed** advisory: when a new advisory is published or the dependency graph changes. Unreviewed advisories don't trigger alerts, and archived repos aren't scanned.

**Severity** reflects impact (CVSS 3.1 or 4.0 based): Low, Medium (Moderate), High, Critical. **EPSS**, from FIRST, is a 0 to 1 probability of exploitation in the next 30 days, with a percentile, refreshed daily.
**Security updates** open PRs that bump to the minimum patched version. PRs are the fix path for dependency alerts.
**Malware alerts** (free) flag packages listed as malicious. Turn on Dependabot alerts first; malware advisories carry no fix version.
Write, Maintain and Admin can view, dismiss and assign Dependabot alerts.
trap: Critical severity in a dev-only tool can wait behind high severity with a high EPSS score in production code.
tryIt: Open github.com/advisories, pick one advisory, and find its severity and EPSS.

details.title: What an alert shows and how to filter
points: Each alert links the affected manifest, the vulnerable package, affected versions and the patched version, with severity and score, CVSS metrics, CWE, CVE ID and GHSA ID.

UI filters: `ecosystem:`, `package:`, `manifest:`, `severity:`, `scope:development`, `has:patch`, `is:open`, `resolution:no-bandwidth`, `relationship:direct`, `epss_percentage:>0.01`. Sort: most-important (default), newest, epss-percentage.

REST filters: `state` open, dismissed, fixed, auto_dismissed; `severity`; `ecosystem` (composer, go, maven, npm, nuget, pip, pub, rubygems, rust); `has=patch`; `epss_percentage` ranges; `sort=epss_percentage`.
Alerts can be assigned to collaborators, teams or a Copilot agent, which opens a draft PR. GitHub Actions dependencies are checked only when pinned by semantic version.

details.title: Security updates
points: Prerequisites: dependency graph and Dependabot alerts on, the dependency in a manifest or lock file, and the repo not archived. Forks get security updates disabled automatically; new repos that qualify get them on.
Enabling opens PRs for every open alert that has a patched version. npm can update a parent or remove a sub-dependency; other ecosystems can't fix an indirect dependency that needs a parent update.

Each PR is authored by dependabot, labelled `dependencies`, named for the package and target version, and signed. A **compatibility score** shows the share of CI runs that passed for the same version jump in other public repos. Merging the PR closes the alert.
Vulnerability details in the PR are hidden from users without alert access. An alert page offers **Create Dependabot security update** when updates aren't enabled.

**Grouped security updates:** one PR per ecosystem, never mixed with version updates; needs graph, alerts and security updates; settings precedence dependabot.yml, then repo UI, then org UI. Repo toggles: Dependabot security updates, Grouped security updates.

details.title: Severity, EPSS and prioritizing
points: Severity answers "how bad if exploited"; EPSS answers "how likely to be exploited soon". Dependency scope (runtime vs development) and whether a patch exists are the other two factors GitHub's alert metrics use.
The security overview Dependabot funnel defaults to `has:patch`, `severity:critical,high`, `epss-percentage:>=0.01`: patchable, severe, and at least 1% likely to be exploited.
Removing a dependency you don't need beats upgrading it: smaller attack surface, less maintenance (module 2).

details.title: Malware alerts
points: Ecosystems: Composer, Go, Maven, npm, NuGet, pip, RubyGems, Rust. Available on GitHub.com and GHES 3.22+.
Malware advisories come from the npm security team and OpenSSF Malicious Packages, are GitHub-reviewed, and have no fix version: remove the package.
Enable Dependabot alerts first, then Dependabot malware alerts. The malware auto-triage preset can dismiss them, which is why it's off by default.

details.title: Notifications
points: No notifications are sent for vulnerabilities found when Dependabot is first enabled on a repo.
Channels: web inbox, email, a CLI warning on push, GitHub Mobile. Email digest: daily or weekly, up to 10 repositories per email. Emails carry an `X-GitHub-Severity` header for filtering.
Default recipients: owners and admins who watch the repo with security alerts or all activity on. Account-wide control: Settings > Notifications > Dependabot alerts.

details.title: If the question follows the training
points: Module 2 says Dependabot alerts aren't on by default, then its summary says Dependabot is on by default for public repos. Today: public repos get alerts on; private repos enable them in Settings > Advanced Security or inherit a configuration.

Module 2 enable paths: personal Settings > Code security; org Settings > Code security and analysis with "Automatically enable for new repositories"; enterprise-level enablement overrides org and repo settings.
Module 2 resolution options: merge the Dependabot PR, select Create Dependabot security update, or Dismiss alert with a reason.

title: Dependabot updates and dependabot.yml
goal: Write a dependabot.yml that groups updates and skips what you don't want.
points: Required keys: `version: 2`, `updates`, `package-ecosystem`, `directory` (or `directories`), `schedule.interval`.
`groups` bundles updates into one PR. With `applies-to: security-updates` a group covers security PRs; without it, version updates.
`ignore` skips dependencies, versions or update types. If allow and ignore both match, ignore wins.
`open-pull-requests-limit` defaults to 5 for version updates. Security updates have a fixed limit of 10. Setting 0 turns version updates off.
`target-branch` affects version updates only. Security updates always target the default branch.
trap: Security updates are switched on in repo settings. The file only tunes them, for example by grouping.
tryIt: Copy the snippet into a scratch file and change the interval to monthly.

snippet.label: .github/dependabot.yml
snippet.code:
version: 2
updates:
  - package-ecosystem: "npm"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
    groups:
      dev-minor-patch:
        dependency-type: "development"
        update-types: ["minor", "patch"]
      security:
        applies-to: security-updates
        patterns: ["*"]
    ignore:
      - dependency-name: "express"
        update-types: ["version-update:semver-major"]

details.title: Schedule
points: `schedule.interval`: daily, weekly (Monday by default), monthly, quarterly, semiannually, yearly (GHES 3.19+), or cron with a `cronjob` value (5 fields or natural language). Optional `day`, `time` (hh:mm), `timezone` (IANA, default UTC); a random time if unset.

`cooldown` delays updates after a release: `default-days` (default 3), `semver-major-days`, `semver-minor-days`, `semver-patch-days`, with `include` and `exclude` lists of up to 150 items. Version updates only.

details.title: Targeting and filtering
points: `allow.dependency-type`: direct, indirect, all, production, development. Indirect works only for bundler, pip, composer, cargo, gomod and uv.
`directories` supports globs; `directory` doesn't. Use `/` for github-actions and devcontainers.
`ignore` takes `dependency-name`, `versions`, `update-types` (`version-update:semver-major|minor|patch`). Ignore wins over allow.
`versioning-strategy`: auto (default), increase, increase-if-necessary, lockfile-only, widen. Apps generally use increase; libraries widen.

`rebase-strategy` only accepts `disabled` (existing PRs still rebase for 30 days). `vendor: true` only for bundler and gomod. `insecure-external-code-execution: allow` for bundler, mix and pip, disabled once registries exist.

details.title: Shaping the pull requests
points: `groups`: `applies-to` version-updates (default) or security-updates; `dependency-type`; `patterns`; `exclude-patterns`; `update-types`. Grouped PR branch names get a 10-character digest. A top-level `multi-ecosystem-groups` key exists too.
`labels` (default `dependencies` plus an ecosystem label; `labels: [ ]` removes all), `milestone` (a number), `assignees`, `reviewers`.
`commit-message`: `prefix` and `prefix-development` up to 50 characters; `include: "scope"` adds deps or deps-dev.
`pull-request-branch-name`: `separator` `/` (default), `-` or `_`; `prefix` default dependabot; `max-length` default 100 (20 to 244); `template` up to 200 characters.

details.title: Ecosystem values
points: `package-ecosystem` values, part 1: bazel, bun, bundler, cargo, composer, conda, deno, devcontainers, docker, docker-compose, dotnet-sdk, elm, gitsubmodule, github-actions, gomod, gradle, helm.
Part 2: julia, maven, mix, nix, npm (also pnpm and yarn), nuget, opentofu, pip (also pipenv and poetry), pre-commit, pub, rust-toolchain, sbt, swift, terraform, uv, vcpkg.
Docker updates scan a Dockerfile's base images; github-actions updates the action versions in your workflows.

details.title: Private registries, secrets and runners
points: `registries`: `type` and `url` required; up to 100 registries and 100 references per updates block; `replaces-base` for mirrors; `scope` only for npm. Declare private registries even when anonymous, because Dependabot jobs run behind an egress allowlist.

**Dependabot secrets:** Settings > Secrets and variables > Dependabot, referenced as `${{secrets.NAME}}`. Names use letters, digits and underscores, no `GITHUB_` prefix, no leading digit. Org secrets need admin and a repository access policy.
GitHub Packages dependencies need no token or registry entry: grant the repo Read access under the package's Manage Actions access.

**Dependabot on Actions runners:** standard hosted and self-hosted runners use no Actions minutes; larger runners are billed. Runner label `dependabot`; labeled runners aren't available on public repos. Dependabot runs bypass Actions policies and disablement.

Runner type: repo Advanced Security > Dependency scanning > Dependabot version updates > Runner type, or org Global settings: Standard GitHub runner or Labeled runner. Org Global settings also hold "Grant Dependabot access to private repositories" (same org only).

details.title: If the question follows the training
points: Module 2 says "the groups option only applies to version updates". That's stale: `applies-to: security-updates` exists. If both answers are offered, grouped security updates are real.

Module 2: Insights > Dependency graph > Dependabot lists monitored files; "Last checked" opens the job log; "Check for updates" reruns it. Forks don't get version updates automatically; use Create config file there.
A user with write permission turns on version updates by committing dependabot.yml; it needs no admin.

title: Auto-triage rules
goal: Cut Dependabot noise with auto-triage rules without losing alerts.
points: Rules run before notifications go out. Auto-dismissed alerts stay filterable and reportable, and reopen if their metadata changes.

**GitHub presets** (free): "Dismiss low impact issues for development-scoped dependencies" (npm dev dependencies; on by default for public repos) and "Dismiss package malware alerts" (off by default).
**Custom rules** (Code Security) can dismiss, snooze until a patch exists, reopen, or open a Dependabot pull request for matching alerts.
Custom rules match on CVE ID, CWE, dependency scope, ecosystem, GHSA ID, manifest path, package name, patch availability, severity and EPSS score.
Use them for known noise, like dev-only tooling, not to hide production risk.
trap: The malware preset can dismiss a truly malicious package. That's why it's off by default.
tryIt: Name one dev-only dependency in a project you know where auto-dismissing low-impact alerts would be safe.

head: Preset
What it dismisses
Default
rows: Dismiss low impact issues for development-scoped dependencies
npm development dependencies with CWEs about resource management, programming and logic errors, or information disclosure
On for public repos; opt-in for private
Alerts where every version of a package is flagged malicious, usually an internal package sharing a name with a malicious public one

details.title: Custom rules
points: Path: Settings > Advanced Security > Dependabot > gear next to Dependabot rules > New rule. Fields: Rule name, State, Target alerts (for example `severity:low`), then the action.

Actions: **Dismiss alerts** (indefinitely, or until a patch is available) and **Open a pull request to resolve this alert**. The PR action is unavailable when dismissing indefinitely or when security updates are already on.
Who: repo admins at repo level; org owners and security managers at org level under Global settings. Up to 10 custom rules per repository during the preview.
Org rules are **Enforced** (repo admins can't edit, disable or delete) or **Enabled** (repo admins can disable). On a conflict the org action wins. Dismissal rules run before PR rules.
Manifest path is a criterion for repo-level rules only.

details.title: Auto-dismissed alerts
points: Find them with the filter `resolution:auto-dismissed`. REST state `auto_dismissed`; GraphQL `AUTO_DISMISSED`; webhook actions `auto_dismissed` and `auto_reopened`.
Auto-reopen triggers: the dependency's scope changes from development to production, or GitHub edits the advisory's metadata.
Audit log: `repository_vulnerability_alert.auto_dismiss` / `auto_reopen`, and `vulnerability_alert_rule.create` / `force_enable`.

title: Dependency review before merge
goal: Block risky dependency changes in pull requests.
points: Dependency review is a **rich diff** on the PR's Files changed tab for manifests and lock files: added, removed and changed dependencies, including indirect ones, with vulnerabilities, licenses, release dates and how many projects use each.
Free on public repos. Private repos need Code Security.

The action fails on `fail-on-severity` (low, moderate, high, critical; default low) and `fail-on-scopes` (runtime by default). By default any vulnerable package fails the check; an undetectable license only warns.
Licenses: `allow-licenses` or `deny-licenses`, never both. The action's README marks `deny-licenses` deprecated, so prefer allow lists.
Make the check required in a ruleset to block merge. Org owners can also enforce the action as a required workflow.
trap: Dependency review prevents new risk. Dependabot security updates fix risk that's already merged.
tryIt: Open the related lab and find the line that blocks high-severity vulnerabilities.

head: Input
Values and default
rows: low, moderate, high, critical; default low
SPDX IDs, mutually exclusive; `deny-licenses` deprecated in the README; not supported on GHES
PURLs whose license check to skip; not supported on GHES
PURLs, or PURL namespaces, to block outright
always, on-failure, never; default never; needs `pull-requests: write`
true makes every failure a warning; overrides `fail-on-severity`; default false
true or false; both default true
false; 120 seconds; for pairing with the submission API
Local path or `OWNER/REPO/FILE@BRANCH`; token for a private config repo
For running on events other than pull_request
List fixed versions in the output

details.title: What the review shows
points: Summary of vulnerable packages, incompatible licenses, invalid SPDX license definitions and unknown licenses (shown as `LicenseRef-clearlydefined-OTHER`). It appears as a PR comment or under Checks > Dependency review.
The rich diff is on the Files changed tab for PRs that change a manifest or lock file, and includes indirect dependencies from lock files.
Dependencies added by the submission API show in dependency review too. Run submission first, then let the action retry while the snapshot-warnings header is set.

details.title: REST and GHES
points: REST: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependency-graph/compare/{basehead}` with `{base}...{head}` and an optional `name` (manifest path). Fields: `change_type` added or removed, `scope` unknown, runtime or development. 403 on a private repo without the product, or on a fork.
GHES: available once the dependency graph is enabled; the action needs Code Security or GHAS on the repo; the license inputs aren't supported.
Disabling Secret Protection and Code Security on a private repo also turns off dependency review.

details.title: If the question follows the training
points: Module 2 setup: Actions tab > New workflow > search "dependency review" > Configure > commit `dependency-review.yml`. The template runs on pull_request to main with `contents: read` and `pull-requests: write`, and sets `comment-summary-in-pr: always`.
Both module examples use `deny-licenses: GPL-1.0-or-later, LGPL-2.0-or-later` as a normal option. Expect it on the exam even though the README deprecates it.
Enforcement in the module: Settings > Branches > Add rule > Require status checks > add `dependency-review`. Today, rulesets are preferred.
The short tag `v4` tracks the latest minor release.

title: Permissions, webhooks and integrations
goal: Route supply chain alerts to the right people and systems.
points: Grant Dependabot alert access to people or teams with write access. Custom roles can add "View Dependabot alerts" and "Dismiss or reopen Dependabot alerts".
Webhook: `dependabot_alert`. The older `repository_vulnerability_alert` event is closing down.
GraphQL: `Repository.vulnerabilityAlerts` returns `RepositoryVulnerabilityAlert` objects. REST: `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependabot/alerts`, plus org and enterprise lists.
Dependabot PRs go through your normal workflow: required reviews, required checks and rulesets apply. A workflow can auto-merge the safe ones.
Who gets notified follows each person's watch and notification settings.
trap: If an answer offers `repository_vulnerability_alert` as the current webhook, it's the old one.
tryIt: Run `gh api "/repos/OWNER/REPO/dependabot/alerts?state=open"` on a repo you own.

head: Event
Actions
rows: assignees_changed, auto_dismissed, auto_reopened, created, dismissed, fixed, reintroduced, reopened, withdrawn
appeared_in_branch, closed_by_user, created, fixed, reopened, reopened_by_user, updated_assignment
created, resolved, reopened, validated, publicly_leaked, assigned, unassigned, metadata_created, metadata_removed

details.title: GraphQL
points: `RepositoryVulnerabilityAlert` fields include `autoDismissedAt`, `dependencyRelationship`, `dependencyScope`, `dismissComment`, `dismissReason`, `fixedAt`, `securityAdvisory`, `securityVulnerability`, `state`, `vulnerableManifestPath`. State enum: AUTO_DISMISSED, DISMISSED, FIXED, OPEN.
Mutation `dismissRepositoryVulnerabilityAlert` takes `repositoryVulnerabilityAlertId` and a `DismissReason`: FIX_STARTED, INACCURATE, NOT_USED, NO_BANDWIDTH, TOLERABLE_RISK.

One endpoint, `POST https://api.github.com/graphql`, with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Nest fields until you reach scalars; `query` is the default root. Resolved alerts aren't stored and can't be retrieved later (module 2).

snippet.label: GraphQL: open vulnerability alerts

details.title: REST
points: List endpoints: `GET /enterprises/{enterprise}/dependabot/alerts`, `GET /orgs/{org}/dependabot/alerts` (owner or security manager), `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependabot/alerts`.

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependabot/alerts/{alert_number}` sets `state`, `dismissed_reason`, `dismissed_comment`, `assignees` and `agent_assignment`. Assignment support is public preview (API version 2026-03-10).
Send `Accept: application/vnd.github+json` and `X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28`. Rate limit: 5,000 requests per hour authenticated, 60 unauthenticated; check with `GET /rate_limit`.

details.title: Org and enterprise settings
points: Org Global settings: "Grant Dependabot access to private repositories" lets Dependabot resolve private same-org dependencies. The docs warn that every org user can then reach that repo's content through Dependabot.
Enterprise policy "Enable or disable Dependabot alerts by repository admins" controls whether repo admins can change the setting.
Audit log: `dependabot_repository_access.*` and `repository_vulnerability_alerts.authorized_users_teams` record access grants.

details.title: Automation patterns (module 2)
points: Auto-merge Dependabot PRs: gate on `github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]'`, run tests, then `gh pr merge --auto --merge "$PR_URL"` with `GH_TOKEN`. Limit it to patch releases.
The Slack and Microsoft Teams apps can post when a Dependabot PR opens, a check fails or an update merges.
Prefer a GitHub App over a personal token for org-wide integrations.
